214: // newAdminHandler reads admin's config and returns an http.Handler suitable
215: // for use in an admin endpoint server, which will be listening on listenAddr.
216: func (admin *AdminConfig) newAdminHandler(addr NetworkAddress, remote bool) adminHandler {
217: 	muxWrap := adminHandler{mux: http.NewServeMux()}
218: 
219: 	// secure the local or remote endpoint respectively
220: 	if remote {
221: 		muxWrap.remoteControl = admin.Remote
222: 	} else {
223: 		muxWrap.enforceHost = !addr.isWildcardInterface()
224: 		muxWrap.allowedOrigins = admin.allowedOrigins(addr)
225: 		muxWrap.enforceOrigin = admin.EnforceOrigin
226: 	}
227: 
228: 	addRouteWithMetrics := func(pattern string, handlerLabel string, h http.Handler) {
229: 		labels := prometheus.Labels{"path": pattern, "handler": handlerLabel}
230: 		h = instrumentHandlerCounter(
231: 			adminMetrics.requestCount.MustCurryWith(labels),
232: 			h,
233: 		)
234: 		muxWrap.mux.Handle(pattern, h)
235: 	}
236: 	// addRoute just calls muxWrap.mux.Handle after
237: 	// wrapping the handler with error handling
238: 	addRoute := func(pattern string, handlerLabel string, h AdminHandler) {
239: 		wrapper := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
240: 			err := h.ServeHTTP(w, r)
241: 			if err != nil {
242: 				labels := prometheus.Labels{
243: 					"path":    pattern,
244: 					"handler": handlerLabel,
245: 					"method":  strings.ToUpper(r.Method),
246: 				}
247: 				adminMetrics.requestErrors.With(labels).Inc()
248: 			}
249: 			muxWrap.handleError(w, r, err)
250: 		})
251: 		addRouteWithMetrics(pattern, handlerLabel, wrapper)
252: 	}
253: 
254: 	const handlerLabel = "admin"
255: 
256: 	// register standard config control endpoints
257: 	addRoute("/"+rawConfigKey+"/", handlerLabel, AdminHandlerFunc(handleConfig))
258: 	addRoute("/id/", handlerLabel, AdminHandlerFunc(handleConfigID))
259: 	addRoute("/stop", handlerLabel, AdminHandlerFunc(handleStop))
260: 
261: 	// register debugging endpoints
262: 	addRouteWithMetrics("/debug/pprof/", handlerLabel, http.HandlerFunc(pprof.Index))
263: 	addRouteWithMetrics("/debug/pprof/cmdline", handlerLabel, http.HandlerFunc(pprof.Cmdline))
264: 	addRouteWithMetrics("/debug/pprof/profile", handlerLabel, http.HandlerFunc(pprof.Profile))
265: 	addRouteWithMetrics("/debug/pprof/symbol", handlerLabel, http.HandlerFunc(pprof.Symbol))
266: 	addRouteWithMetrics("/debug/pprof/trace", handlerLabel, http.HandlerFunc(pprof.Trace))
267: 	addRouteWithMetrics("/debug/vars", handlerLabel, expvar.Handler())
268: 
269: 	// register third-party module endpoints
270: 	for _, m := range GetModules("admin.api") {
271: 		router := m.New().(AdminRouter)
272: 		handlerLabel := m.ID.Name()
273: 		for _, route := range router.Routes() {
274: 			addRoute(route.Pattern, handlerLabel, route.Handler)
275: 		}
276: 		admin.routers = append(admin.routers, router)
277: 	}
278: 
279: 	return muxWrap
280: }

303: // allowedOrigins returns a list of origins that are allowed.
304: // If admin.Origins is nil (null), the provided listen address
305: // will be used as the default origin. If admin.Origins is
306: // empty, no origins will be allowed, effectively bricking the
307: // endpoint for non-unix-socket endpoints, but whatever.
308: func (admin AdminConfig) allowedOrigins(addr NetworkAddress) []*url.URL {
309: 	uniqueOrigins := make(map[string]struct{})
310: 	for _, o := range admin.Origins {
311: 		uniqueOrigins[o] = struct{}{}
312: 	}
313: 	if admin.Origins == nil {
314: 		if addr.isLoopback() {
315: 			if addr.IsUnixNetwork() {
316: 				// RFC 2616, Section 14.26:
317: 				// "A client MUST include a Host header field in all HTTP/1.1 request
318: 				// messages. If the requested URI does not include an Internet host
319: 				// name for the service being requested, then the Host header field MUST
320: 				// be given with an empty value."
321: 				//
322: 				// UPDATE July 2023: Go broke this by patching a minor security bug in 1.20.6.
323: 				// Understandable, but frustrating. See:
324: 				// https://github.com/golang/go/issues/60374
325: 				// See also the discussion here:
326: 				// https://github.com/golang/go/issues/61431
327: 				//
328: 				// We can no longer conform to RFC 2616 Section 14.26 from either Go or curl
329: 				// in purity. (Curl allowed no host between 7.40 and 7.50, but now requires a
330: 				// bogus host; see https://superuser.com/a/925610.) If we disable Host/Origin
331: 				// security checks, the infosec community assures me that it is secure to do
332: 				// so, because:
333: 				// 1) Browsers do not allow access to unix sockets
334: 				// 2) DNS is irrelevant to unix sockets
335: 				//
336: 				// I am not quite ready to trust either of those external factors, so instead
337: 				// of disabling Host/Origin checks, we now allow specific Host values when
338: 				// accessing the admin endpoint over unix sockets. I definitely don't trust
339: 				// DNS (e.g. I don't trust 'localhost' to always resolve to the local host),
340: 				// and IP shouldn't even be used, but if it is for some reason, I think we can
341: 				// at least be reasonably assured that 127.0.0.1 and ::1 route to the local
342: 				// machine, meaning that a hypothetical browser origin would have to be on the
343: 				// local machine as well.
344: 				uniqueOrigins[""] = struct{}{}
345: 				uniqueOrigins["127.0.0.1"] = struct{}{}
346: 				uniqueOrigins["::1"] = struct{}{}
347: 			} else {
348: 				uniqueOrigins[net.JoinHostPort("localhost", addr.port())] = struct{}{}
349: 				uniqueOrigins[net.JoinHostPort("::1", addr.port())] = struct{}{}
350: 				uniqueOrigins[net.JoinHostPort("127.0.0.1", addr.port())] = struct{}{}
351: 			}
352: 		}
353: 		if !addr.IsUnixNetwork() {
354: 			uniqueOrigins[addr.JoinHostPort(0)] = struct{}{}
355: 		}
356: 	}
357: 	allowed := make([]*url.URL, 0, len(uniqueOrigins))
358: 	for originStr := range uniqueOrigins {
359: 		var origin *url.URL
360: 		if strings.Contains(originStr, "://") {
361: 			var err error
362: 			origin, err = url.Parse(originStr)
363: 			if err != nil {
364: 				continue
365: 			}
366: 			origin.Path = ""
367: 			origin.RawPath = ""
368: 			origin.Fragment = ""
369: 			origin.RawFragment = ""
370: 			origin.RawQuery = ""
371: 		} else {
372: 			origin = &url.URL{Host: originStr}
373: 		}
374: 		allowed = append(allowed, origin)
375: 	}
376: 	return allowed
377: }

379: // replaceLocalAdminServer replaces the running local admin server
380: // according to the relevant configuration in cfg. If no configuration
381: // for the admin endpoint exists in cfg, a default one is used, so
382: // that there is always an admin server (unless it is explicitly
383: // configured to be disabled).
384: func replaceLocalAdminServer(cfg *Config) error {
385: 	// always* be sure to close down the old admin endpoint
386: 	// as gracefully as possible, even if the new one is
387: 	// disabled -- careful to use reference to the current
388: 	// (old) admin endpoint since it will be different
389: 	// when the function returns
390: 	// (* except if the new one fails to start)
391: 	oldAdminServer := localAdminServer
392: 	var err error
393: 	defer func() {
394: 		// do the shutdown asynchronously so that any
395: 		// current API request gets a response; this
396: 		// goroutine may last a few seconds
397: 		if oldAdminServer != nil && err == nil {
398: 			go func(oldAdminServer *http.Server) {
399: 				err := stopAdminServer(oldAdminServer)
400: 				if err != nil {
401: 					Log().Named("admin").Error("stopping current admin endpoint", zap.Error(err))
402: 				}
403: 			}(oldAdminServer)
404: 		}
405: 	}()
406: 
407: 	// set a default if admin wasn't otherwise configured
408: 	if cfg.Admin == nil {
409: 		cfg.Admin = &AdminConfig{
410: 			Listen: DefaultAdminListen,
411: 		}
412: 	}
413: 
414: 	// if new admin endpoint is to be disabled, we're done
415: 	if cfg.Admin.Disabled {
416: 		Log().Named("admin").Warn("admin endpoint disabled")
417: 		return nil
418: 	}
419: 
420: 	// extract a singular listener address
421: 	addr, err := parseAdminListenAddr(cfg.Admin.Listen, DefaultAdminListen)
422: 	if err != nil {
423: 		return err
424: 	}
425: 
426: 	handler := cfg.Admin.newAdminHandler(addr, false)
427: 
428: 	ln, err := addr.Listen(context.TODO(), 0, net.ListenConfig{})
429: 	if err != nil {
430: 		return err
431: 	}
432: 
433: 	serverMu.Lock()
434: 	localAdminServer = &http.Server{
435: 		Addr:              addr.String(), // for logging purposes only
436: 		Handler:           handler,
437: 		ReadTimeout:       10 * time.Second,
438: 		ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
439: 		IdleTimeout:       60 * time.Second,
440: 		MaxHeaderBytes:    1024 * 64,
441: 	}
442: 	serverMu.Unlock()
443: 
444: 	adminLogger := Log().Named("admin")
445: 	go func() {
446: 		serverMu.Lock()
447: 		server := localAdminServer
448: 		serverMu.Unlock()
449: 		if err := server.Serve(ln.(net.Listener)); !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
450: 			adminLogger.Error("admin server shutdown for unknown reason", zap.Error(err))
451: 		}
452: 	}()
453: 
454: 	adminLogger.Info("admin endpoint started",
455: 		zap.String("address", addr.String()),
456: 		zap.Bool("enforce_origin", cfg.Admin.EnforceOrigin),
457: 		zap.Array("origins", loggableURLArray(handler.allowedOrigins)))
458: 
459: 	if !handler.enforceHost {
460: 		adminLogger.Warn("admin endpoint on open interface; host checking disabled",
461: 			zap.String("address", addr.String()))
462: 	}
463: 
464: 	return nil
465: }

515: // replaceRemoteAdminServer replaces the running remote admin server
516: // according to the relevant configuration in cfg. It stops any previous
517: // remote admin server and only starts a new one if configured.
518: func replaceRemoteAdminServer(ctx Context, cfg *Config) error {
519: 	if cfg == nil {
520: 		return nil
521: 	}
522: 
523: 	remoteLogger := Log().Named("admin.remote")
524: 
525: 	oldAdminServer := remoteAdminServer
526: 	defer func() {
527: 		if oldAdminServer != nil {
528: 			go func(oldAdminServer *http.Server) {
529: 				err := stopAdminServer(oldAdminServer)
530: 				if err != nil {
531: 					Log().Named("admin").Error("stopping current secure admin endpoint", zap.Error(err))
532: 				}
533: 			}(oldAdminServer)
534: 		}
535: 	}()
536: 
537: 	if cfg.Admin == nil || cfg.Admin.Remote == nil {
538: 		return nil
539: 	}
540: 
541: 	addr, err := parseAdminListenAddr(cfg.Admin.Remote.Listen, DefaultRemoteAdminListen)
542: 	if err != nil {
543: 		return err
544: 	}
545: 
546: 	// make the HTTP handler but disable Host/Origin enforcement
547: 	// because we are using TLS authentication instead
548: 	handler := cfg.Admin.newAdminHandler(addr, true)
549: 
550: 	// create client certificate pool for TLS mutual auth, and extract public keys
551: 	// so that we can enforce access controls at the application layer
552: 	clientCertPool := x509.NewCertPool()
553: 	for i, accessControl := range cfg.Admin.Remote.AccessControl {
554: 		for j, certBase64 := range accessControl.PublicKeys {
555: 			cert, err := decodeBase64DERCert(certBase64)
556: 			if err != nil {
557: 				return fmt.Errorf("access control %d public key %d: parsing base64 certificate DER: %v", i, j, err)
558: 			}
559: 			accessControl.publicKeys = append(accessControl.publicKeys, cert.PublicKey)
560: 			clientCertPool.AddCert(cert)
561: 		}
562: 	}
563: 
564: 	// create TLS config that will enforce mutual authentication
565: 	if identityCertCache == nil {
566: 		return fmt.Errorf("cannot enable remote admin without a certificate cache; configure identity management to initialize a certificate cache")
567: 	}
568: 	cmCfg := cfg.Admin.Identity.certmagicConfig(remoteLogger, false)
569: 	tlsConfig := cmCfg.TLSConfig()
570: 	tlsConfig.NextProtos = nil // this server does not solve ACME challenges
571: 	tlsConfig.ClientAuth = tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert
572: 	tlsConfig.ClientCAs = clientCertPool
573: 
574: 	// convert logger to stdlib so it can be used by HTTP server
575: 	serverLogger, err := zap.NewStdLogAt(remoteLogger, zap.DebugLevel)
576: 	if err != nil {
577: 		return err
578: 	}
579: 
580: 	serverMu.Lock()
581: 	// create secure HTTP server
582: 	remoteAdminServer = &http.Server{
583: 		Addr:              addr.String(), // for logging purposes only
584: 		Handler:           handler,
585: 		TLSConfig:         tlsConfig,
586: 		ReadTimeout:       10 * time.Second,
587: 		ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
588: 		IdleTimeout:       60 * time.Second,
589: 		MaxHeaderBytes:    1024 * 64,
590: 		ErrorLog:          serverLogger,
591: 	}
592: 	serverMu.Unlock()
593: 
594: 	// start listener
595: 	lnAny, err := addr.Listen(ctx, 0, net.ListenConfig{})
596: 	if err != nil {
597: 		return err
598: 	}
599: 	ln := lnAny.(net.Listener)
600: 	ln = tls.NewListener(ln, tlsConfig)
601: 
602: 	go func() {
603: 		serverMu.Lock()
604: 		server := remoteAdminServer
605: 		serverMu.Unlock()
606: 		if err := server.Serve(ln); !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
607: 			remoteLogger.Error("admin remote server shutdown for unknown reason", zap.Error(err))
608: 		}
609: 	}()
610: 
611: 	remoteLogger.Info("secure admin remote control endpoint started",
612: 		zap.String("address", addr.String()))
613: 
614: 	return nil
615: }

658: // enforceAccessControls enforces application-layer access controls for r based on remote.
659: // It expects that the TLS server has already established at least one verified chain of
660: // trust, and then looks for a matching, authorized public key that is allowed to access
661: // the defined path(s) using the defined method(s).
662: func (remote RemoteAdmin) enforceAccessControls(r *http.Request) error {
663: 	for _, chain := range r.TLS.VerifiedChains {
664: 		for _, peerCert := range chain {
665: 			for _, adminAccess := range remote.AccessControl {
666: 				for _, allowedKey := range adminAccess.publicKeys {
667: 					// see if we found a matching public key; the TLS server already verified the chain
668: 					// so we know the client possesses the associated private key; this handy interface
669: 					// doesn't appear to be defined anywhere in the std lib, but was implemented here:
670: 					// https://github.com/golang/go/commit/b5f2c0f50297fa5cd14af668ddd7fd923626cf8c
671: 					comparer, ok := peerCert.PublicKey.(interface{ Equal(crypto.PublicKey) bool })
672: 					if !ok || !comparer.Equal(allowedKey) {
673: 						continue
674: 					}
675: 
676: 					// key recognized; make sure its HTTP request is permitted
677: 					for _, accessPerm := range adminAccess.Permissions {
678: 						// verify method
679: 						methodFound := accessPerm.Methods == nil
680: 						for _, method := range accessPerm.Methods {
681: 							if method == r.Method {
682: 								methodFound = true
683: 								break
684: 							}
685: 						}
686: 						if !methodFound {
687: 							return APIError{
688: 								HTTPStatus: http.StatusForbidden,
689: 								Message:    "not authorized to use this method",
690: 							}
691: 						}
692: 
693: 						// verify path
694: 						pathFound := accessPerm.Paths == nil
695: 						for _, allowedPath := range accessPerm.Paths {
696: 							if strings.HasPrefix(r.URL.Path, allowedPath) {
697: 								pathFound = true
698: 								break
699: 							}
700: 						}
701: 						if !pathFound {
702: 							return APIError{
703: 								HTTPStatus: http.StatusForbidden,
704: 								Message:    "not authorized to access this path",
705: 							}
706: 						}
707: 					}
708: 
709: 					// public key authorized, method and path allowed
710: 					return nil
711: 				}
712: 			}
713: 		}
714: 	}
715: 
716: 	// in theory, this should never happen; with an unverified chain, the TLS server
717: 	// should not accept the connection in the first place, and the acceptable cert
718: 	// pool is configured using the same list of public keys we verify against
719: 	return APIError{
720: 		HTTPStatus: http.StatusUnauthorized,
721: 		Message:    "client identity not authorized",
722: 	}
723: }

792: // serveHTTP is the internal entry point for API requests. It may
793: // be called more than once per request, for example if a request
794: // is rewritten (i.e. internal redirect).
795: func (h adminHandler) serveHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
796: 	if h.remoteControl != nil {
797: 		// enforce access controls on secure endpoint
798: 		if err := h.remoteControl.enforceAccessControls(r); err != nil {
799: 			h.handleError(w, r, err)
800: 			return
801: 		}
802: 	}
803: 
804: 	if strings.Contains(r.Header.Get("Upgrade"), "websocket") {
805: 		// I've never been able demonstrate a vulnerability myself, but apparently
806: 		// WebSocket connections originating from browsers aren't subject to CORS
807: 		// restrictions, so we'll just be on the safe side
808: 		h.handleError(w, r, fmt.Errorf("websocket connections aren't allowed"))
809: 		return
810: 	}
811: 
812: 	if h.enforceHost {
813: 		// DNS rebinding mitigation
814: 		err := h.checkHost(r)
815: 		if err != nil {
816: 			h.handleError(w, r, err)
817: 			return
818: 		}
819: 	}
820: 
821: 	if h.enforceOrigin {
822: 		// cross-site mitigation
823: 		origin, err := h.checkOrigin(r)
824: 		if err != nil {
825: 			h.handleError(w, r, err)
826: 			return
827: 		}
828: 
829: 		if r.Method == http.MethodOptions {
830: 			w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "OPTIONS, GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE")
831: 			w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "Content-Type, Content-Length, Cache-Control")
832: 			w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Credentials", "true")
833: 		}
834: 		w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", origin)
835: 	}
836: 
837: 	h.mux.ServeHTTP(w, r)
838: }

841: 	if err == nil {
842: 		return

845: 		h.serveHTTP(w, r)
846: 		return

849: 	apiErr, ok := err.(APIError)
850: 	if !ok {
851: 		apiErr = APIError{
852: 			HTTPStatus: http.StatusInternalServerError,
853: 			Err:        err,
854: 		}

856: 	if apiErr.HTTPStatus == 0 {

860: 		apiErr.Message = apiErr.Err.Error()

957: func handleConfig(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) error {
958: 	switch r.Method {
959: 	case http.MethodGet:
960: 		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
961: 		// Set the ETag as a trailer header.
962: 		// The alternative is to write the config to a buffer, and
963: 		// then hash that.
964: 		w.Header().Set("Trailer", "ETag")
965: 
966: 		hash := etagHasher()
967: 		configWriter := io.MultiWriter(w, hash)
968: 		err := readConfig(r.URL.Path, configWriter)
969: 		if err != nil {
970: 			return APIError{HTTPStatus: http.StatusBadRequest, Err: err}
971: 		}
972: 
973: 		// we could consider setting up a sync.Pool for the summed
974: 		// hashes to reduce GC pressure.
975: 		w.Header().Set("Etag", makeEtag(r.URL.Path, hash))
976: 
977: 		return nil
978: 
979: 	case http.MethodPost,
980: 		http.MethodPut,
981: 		http.MethodPatch,
982: 		http.MethodDelete:
983: 
984: 		// DELETE does not use a body, but the others do
985: 		var body []byte
986: 		if r.Method != http.MethodDelete {
987: 			if ct := r.Header.Get("Content-Type"); !strings.Contains(ct, "/json") {
988: 				return APIError{
989: 					HTTPStatus: http.StatusBadRequest,
990: 					Err:        fmt.Errorf("unacceptable content-type: %v; 'application/json' required", ct),
991: 				}
992: 			}
993: 
994: 			buf := bufPool.Get().(*bytes.Buffer)
995: 			buf.Reset()
996: 			defer bufPool.Put(buf)
997: 
998: 			_, err := io.Copy(buf, r.Body)
999: 			if err != nil {
1000: 				return APIError{
1001: 					HTTPStatus: http.StatusBadRequest,
1002: 					Err:        fmt.Errorf("reading request body: %v", err),
1003: 				}
1004: 			}
1005: 			body = buf.Bytes()
1006: 		}
1007: 
1008: 		forceReload := r.Header.Get("Cache-Control") == "must-revalidate"
1009: 
1010: 		err := changeConfig(r.Method, r.URL.Path, body, r.Header.Get("If-Match"), forceReload)
1011: 		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, errSameConfig) {
1012: 			return err
1013: 		}
1014: 
1015: 	default:
1016: 		return APIError{
1017: 			HTTPStatus: http.StatusMethodNotAllowed,
1018: 			Err:        fmt.Errorf("method %s not allowed", r.Method),
1019: 		}
1020: 	}
1021: 
1022: 	return nil
1023: }

1073: // unsyncedConfigAccess traverses into the current config and performs
1074: // the operation at path according to method, using body and out as
1075: // needed. This is a low-level, unsynchronized function; most callers
1076: // will want to use changeConfig or readConfig instead. This requires a
1077: // read or write lock on currentCtxMu, depending on method (GET needs
1078: // only a read lock; all others need a write lock).
1079: func unsyncedConfigAccess(method, path string, body []byte, out io.Writer) error {
1080: 	var err error
1081: 	var val any
1082: 
1083: 	canon := canonicalHTTPMethod(method)
1084: 
1085: 	// if there is a request body, decode it into the
1086: 	// variable that will be set in the config according
1087: 	// to method and path
1088: 	if len(body) > 0 {
1089: 		payload := append([]byte(nil), body...)
1090: 		err = json.Unmarshal(payload, &val)
1091: 		if err != nil {
1092: 			return fmt.Errorf("decoding request body: %v", err)
1093: 		}
1094: 	}
1095: 
1096: 	enc := json.NewEncoder(out)
1097: 	enc.SetIndent("", "")
1098: 
1099: 	pathText := ToString(path)
1100: 	cleanPath := strings.Trim(pathText, "/")
1101: 	if cleanPath == "" {
1102: 		return fmt.Errorf("no traversable path")
1103: 	}
1104: 
1105: 	parts := strings.Split(cleanPath, "/")
1106: 
1107: 	// A path that ends with "..." implies:
1108: 	// 1) the part before it is an array
1109: 	// 2) the payload is an array
1110: 	// and means that the user wants to expand the elements
1111: 	// in the payload array and append each one into the
1112: 	// destination array, like so:
